% parity: one page of justified prose at a fully declared geometry; every level is expected to hold, so a failure here is the engine changing
% Floor probe. Page size, margins, body size and the paragraph gap are all
% declared on both sides, and the reference declares them in big points,
% which is what the engine measures in, so neither point unit takes part.
% Micro-typography is declared off here because the reference loads no
% microtype: left at the engine's default, protrusion and expansion set
% every line at its own horizontal scale, which the placement level would
% read as a difference neither half declared. Measured 2026-09-25: turning
% them off moves no level this ladder has, and takes the placement p95
% from 1.58 to 1.32 bp.
\documentclass{article}
\page{ size = letter, margin = 1in, fontsize = 10pt, measure = free, protrusion = off, expansion = off }
\fonts{ body = "Open Sans" }
\begin{document}
The harbour office keeps two ledgers, and the clerk who reconciles them
each morning has never once found them to agree before noon. One counts
hulls; the other counts berths. A hull may wait outside the wall for a
week, and a berth may stand empty while its tenant is repaired, so the two
numbers drift apart by the ordinary working of the port rather than by
anyone's error.

Write to the harbourmaster at berths@example.org if a discrepancy matters
to you. The reply will quote both ledgers and decline to prefer either,
which is the correct answer and rarely the useful one.
\end{document}
